record.paper_title: Open problems on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary
record.context_brief: volume threshold for crossing the boundary plane
record.original_question: Let C be a non-circular closed convex planar curve. Does there exist a threshold volume V_C > 0, depending only on C, such that every compact embedded constant-mean-curvature disk Σ spanning C with enclosed volume V satisfies the following trichotomy: (i) if V ≤ V_C, then Σ lies on one side of the boundary plane P; (ii) if V = V_C, then Σ is tangent to P at the points of minimum curvature of C; and (iii) if V > V_C, then Σ has points on both sides of P?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.7. Let C be a non-circular closed convex planar curve. Prove that there is V_C>0 depending only on C such that, if Σ is a compact cmc embedded disk spanning C and with volume V>0, it holds: (1) If V\leq V_C, then Σ lies in one side of P. (2) If V=V_C, then Σ is tangent to P at the points of minimum curvature of C. (3) If V>V_C, then Σ has points in both sides of P.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in a recent survey on compact CMC surfaces with boundary (2025). No published resolution was found; the question concerning a volume threshold characterizing when a CMC disk spanning a non-circular convex curve must lie on one side of its boundary plane appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 3.7 poses the existence of a threshold volume V_C for non-circular convex boundary curves governing when CMC disks cross the boundary plane.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as open in a 2025 survey of open problems on compact CMC surfaces with boundary.
